final_rationale: The verdict does not change because the Actor provided no new admissible evidence and instead reframed the same record more narrowly. That reframing is useful but not curative. A caveated argument that certification is 'arguable' is different from evidence that certification is compliant under the governing policy. Here, the unresolved compliance predicate remains: the available policy text makes the weakness material when it affects a named launch use case, and says non-core or low-volume product labels do not resolve materiality when legal review is pending. The Actor concedes both the named-use-case fact pattern and the open legal review. On this record, a narrowed, caveated certification rationale may describe litigation or governance posture, but it does not establish policy compliance. Business-cost arguments and monitoring-oriented public guidance likewise do not replace the missing internal policy resolution. The appropriate final assessment therefore remains noncompliant, with escalation warranted.
remaining_concerns: The policy text states a weakness is material if it affects a named launch use case, and the affected hazmat documentation segment is still described as named in two freight rollout commitments.
The same policy text states non-core or low-volume labels do not resolve materiality when legal review is pending, and legal review remains open on disclosure.
Aggregate readiness passing and the absence of severity-one rehearsal incidents do not satisfy the separate materiality and disclosure predicate under the stated policy.

The actor's narrowed position shows the certification defense is arguable and contestable, but it does not supply admissible evidence of formal policy resolution, legal clearance, or explicit approval to certify despite the known segment miss.
